title: Why Do Northern Europeans Have Light Eyes?
excerpt: Every blue-eyed person alive today descends from one ancestor who carried a single mutation 6,000-10,000 years ago. Here is the genetics, the physics, and the evolution behind Europe's lightest eyes.

title: What Is a Phenotype - and Why It Is Not a Race
excerpt: Phenotype is a century-old scientific term for observable traits, not a synonym for race. The difference matters: clines, Lewontin's 85 percent, and how to read human variation honestly.
image_alt: Huanghoid phenotype average face composite from East Asia

title: The Evolutionary Story Behind Andean Faces
excerpt: From round, heat-conserving faces above 3,500 meters to mixed-mestizo lowland populations, the skulls of the Andes are a lesson in adaptation pushed to its current edge.
image_alt: North Andid phenotype average face composite from the South American Andes

title: How Average Face Composites Are Made
excerpt: An average face is not a real face. It is a statistical average of hundreds of aligned photographs - and that is exactly why it is so good at describing population patterns.
image_alt: A composite human face built from an aligned set of phenotype photographs
